html:
The Battle of Marj Dabiq was fought on 24 August 1516 on a plain north of Aleppo. The Ottoman army of Sultan Selim I destroyed the army of the Mamluk Sultanate, whose old sultan, Qansuh al-Ghawri, died on the field.

The Ottomans had guns and trained infantry, while the Mamluks trusted to their famous cavalry. Some Mamluk governors changed sides during the battle. Aleppo and Damascus opened their gates, and the next year Selim took Egypt (Ottomans conquer Egypt).

Syria stayed under the Ottoman Empire for four hundred years, until 1918. Aleppo grew into one of the great trading cities of the empire.
